bullets.title: NVDA: Invests $5B in Ilya Sutskever's Safe Superintelligence (SSI); Korea supply chain deepens
bullets.body: NVIDIA announced a multi-billion dollar investment (widely cited as ~$5B) in Ilya Sutskever's Safe Superintelligence startup, with SSI gaining long-term access to next-gen Vera chips. Separately, Korea's $950B AI summit locked Samsung and SK Hynix deeper into NVIDIA's supply chain, and NVIDIA also committed $1B to invest in NAVER Corp. On the day, NVDA options flow was described as the most bearish of major names, and NVDA has turned negative for the month even as Apple reclaimed the largest-company title (~$4.95T vs NVDA's ~$4.81T).

bullets.title: NVDA/MSFT: Launch open AI security alliance excluding OpenAI, Google, Anthropic
bullets.body: Satya Nadella and Jensen Huang announced a joint open AI security alliance focused on the frontier AI ecosystem. Notably, the alliance excludes OpenAI, Google, and Anthropic—a competitive signal worth watching heading into this week's earnings.

bullets.title: MSFT: Copilot sales beat in FY26Q4; Azure capacity/pricing trends positive ahead of earnings
bullets.body: A sell-side preview flagged that Microsoft's FY26Q4 Copilot sales likely beat prior expectations, user experience is improving, and Azure capacity and pricing trends are positive—offset by intense AI competition. Separately, market chatter flagged investor worry that Microsoft may cut capex, though the Copilot beat thesis runs counter to that concern.

bullets.title: Semis -4% vs. Software +3%: Sharp sector unwind underway; chip valuations flagged as above dot-com peak
bullets.body: Semiconductor stocks reversed a 1%+ opening gain to trade down ~4% on the day—led by China DUV news—while software (IGV) rallied ~3%. Multiple commentators flagged that US chipmaker valuations now exceed dot-com bubble peaks and that NAND price weakness is a canary in the AI trade. MU fell 6.1% to below $1T market cap. One analyst argued the China DUV panic is overblown and suggested buying the dip in chip stocks.

bullets.title: China DUV mass production: Goldman warns 'memory has a new problem'; ASML -6-8%
bullets.body: The Information reported China has started mass-producing homegrown DUV lithography tools, with initial targets of 5 machines this year scaling to 20 by 2027. Goldman warned this creates a new problem for the memory industry. ASML shares were halted and reopened down 7-8%; BESI also dropped 7-8%. One semi-industry contact argued the development changes nothing for long-term WFE demand (>$300B by 2030) and that DUV demand is additive not subtractive.

bullets.title: TSLA: Deutsche Bank cuts PT to $420 (from $465), maintains Buy; Elon buyback thesis questioned
bullets.body: Deutsche Bank's Edison Yu trimmed his Tesla price target to $420 from $465, keeping a Buy rating. Separately, social commentary suggested Elon is unlikely to repeat his September stock purchase (which boosted morale for the comp package) given changed circumstances. TSLA is trading at the same level as one year ago and October 2021—five years of no net price progress.

bullets.title: AAPL reclaims world's largest company at ~$4.95T; up 16% MTD vs NVDA down MTD
bullets.body: Apple moved back ahead of NVIDIA as the world's largest company by market cap (~$4.95T vs ~$4.81T). AAPL has rallied ~16% month-to-date while NVDA has turned negative for July. AAPL reports earnings this week.

bullets.title: AMZN: $4B compute deal with Pinterest on AWS Trainium; LEO satellite network (5,105 sats) planned for 2028
bullets.body: Amazon signed a $4B long-term compute deal with Pinterest using AWS Trainium chips—seen as evidence the compute bottleneck is being underappreciated vs. the semiconductor bottleneck. Separately, Amazon LEO proposed a new constellation of up to 5,105 satellites for direct mobile connectivity, with deployment beginning 2028.

bullets.title: META/GOOGL/AMZN: Moody's warns 'unprecedented' AI capex threatens credit quality; Mark Cuban pickleball court warning
bullets.body: Moody's flagged that 'unprecedented' AI spending by Amazon, Meta, and Alphabet threatens their credit quality. Mark Cuban echoed the overcapacity risk, warning that data centers built on hundreds of billions in borrowed capital could become 'pickleball courts.' Hyperscaler capex is projected to hit $1.4T by 2028 (from $426B in 2025). Macro overlay: Goldman's quant desk separately flagged rising real-rate pressure and policy reflexivity concerns around hyperscaler debt.

bullets.title: GOOGL: Climbs back above $4T market cap; YouTube Premium to bundle Peacock starting 2025
bullets.body: Google reclaimed $4T market cap intraday. Separately, YouTube TV and Peacock signed a new content distribution deal making all Peacock content (including live sports) available to YouTube Premium subscribers in the US, launching in early 2025—a meaningful content value-add for YouTube's subscription business.

bullets.title: NOW/GOOGL: Memory pullback seen as overreaction; NOW 2Q26 pull-forward and GCP ROI inflection flagged as bullish
bullets.body: One sell-side weekly noted the Kimi K3 KV cache-driven memory selloff looks like an overreaction, and highlighted two bullish single-stock setups: ServiceNow pulling forward 2Q26 demand, and Google Cloud Platform showing a return-on-investment inflection.

bullets.title: SNDK: Down $1,000+ from June 25 ATH; Total Return Swap meltup unwinds
bullets.body: SNDK has fallen more than $1,000 from its June 25 all-time high, which was described as the result of a historic Total Return Swap meltup. The unwind is continuing—one trader posted a triple-down-arrow on the name today.

bullets.title: INTC: Intel 18A-P and 14A secure Cadence's full EDA toolchain
bullets.body: Intel's 18A-P and 14A advanced process nodes gained access to Cadence's complete EDA toolchain, tightening the ecosystem around Intel Foundry and signaling Cadence's confidence in Intel's manufacturing capability as it challenges TSMC's foundry leadership.

bullets.title: ADBE: Recovers full 10.5% decline from 7/17–7/23 in just two trading days
bullets.body: Adobe recovered its entire 10.5% selloff (July 17–23) over the last two trading sessions, a notable technical reversal worth monitoring heading into the broader mega-cap earnings week.

bullets.title: HOOD: Robinhood cut 290 staff (10%) in broader crypto sector restructuring
bullets.body: Robinhood announced 290 layoffs representing ~10% of its workforce, disclosed in the context of broader crypto sector stress. Coinbase also cut 500 employees (14%). HOOD reports earnings this week.

bullets.title: PSKY/WBD: LightShed analyst says acquisition 'devolved into multiyear mess'
bullets.body: LightShed analyst characterized the PSKY acquisition of WBD as a deal that made sense for scale at the time but has since become a multiyear problem—no specific rating action noted but directionally negative framing ahead of any catalyst.

bullets.title: NOK: Insiders voluntarily buy ~$1.6M in shares on July 24
bullets.body: Nokia insiders made voluntary open-market purchases of approximately $1.585M in shares on Friday, July 24—distinct from compensation-related transactions—signaling insider confidence in the name.

bullets.title: SPOT: Spotify acknowledges unspecified technical issues
bullets.body: Spotify flagged awareness of unspecified platform issues and said it was investigating. No further financial or operational details disclosed, but worth monitoring for any service disruption headlines.

bullets.title: Mega-cap earnings week: AMZN, META, MSFT, AAPL, GOOGL all reporting; FOMC Wednesday
bullets.body: This is the busiest earnings week of the quarter with all five Mag-7 companies reporting. Macro overlay includes Wednesday's FOMC (futures pricing ~36% odds of a hike), PCE, and GDP data. Goldman warns macro risks (inflation, real rates) are rising and markets may be mispricing geopolitical and rate volatility.
